question: In a common rail diesel injection system, what is the primary function of the pressure relief valve located on the common rail?
options: To regulate fuel temperature by releasing excess heat
To limit maximum rail pressure and protect system components from overpressure
To control the quantity of fuel delivered to each injector
To recirculate fuel back to the injection pump for re-pressurisation

question: When diagnosing an engine with excessive crankcase pressure (blow-by), which combination of symptoms would MOST likely confirm worn piston rings as the primary cause?
options: Blue exhaust smoke under load, oil consumption, and positive crankcase ventilation valve stuck closed
White exhaust smoke at startup, coolant loss, and overheating
Black exhaust smoke at idle, rich air-fuel mixture, and high fuel consumption
Grey exhaust smoke, misfires, and catalytic converter failure

question: A vehicle with an electronically controlled automatic transmission exhibits harsh upshifts under light throttle but smooth shifts under heavy throttle. Which component is MOST likely faulty?
options: Torque converter clutch solenoid
Throttle position sensor providing incorrect load signal to the TCM
Line pressure solenoid causing consistently low hydraulic pressure
Output shaft speed sensor giving erratic signals

question: In an ABS system, during a wheel lock-up event, what is the correct sequence of solenoid valve operations in the hydraulic modulator?
options: Inlet valve closes, outlet valve opens (pressure decrease), then inlet closes and outlet closes (pressure hold), then inlet opens (pressure increase)
Inlet valve opens, outlet valve opens (pressure increase), then both close (pressure hold)
Outlet valve closes, inlet valve opens, then both valves cycle rapidly
Inlet valve opens, outlet valve closes, then inlet closes and outlet opens

question: A technician measures 450 mV at the upstream oxygen sensor of a port-injected petrol engine at idle. This reading indicates which condition?
options: A rich air-fuel mixture with low oxygen content in the exhaust
A lean air-fuel mixture with high oxygen content in the exhaust
A stoichiometric mixture of exactly 14.7:1
A faulty sensor that requires immediate replacement

question: Which type of vehicle network protocol operates at speeds up to 1 Mbit/s and is primarily used for powertrain and chassis control modules requiring fast, real-time data exchange?
options: LIN (Local Interconnect Network)
MOST (Media Oriented Systems Transport)
CAN (Controller Area Network) High Speed
K-Line (ISO 9141)

question: When performing a cylinder contribution test on a diesel engine using a scan tool, a cylinder that shows a LARGE increase in engine speed when it is disabled indicates what condition?
options: That cylinder is contributing excessively and may have a stuck-open injector or high injector delivery
That cylinder has no contribution due to a failed injector
That cylinder has a compression fault causing misfires
That the fuel pressure regulator is not maintaining correct rail pressure

question: In a MacPherson strut front suspension system, what is the effect of increasing the strut top mount offset towards the vehicle centre-line?
options: It increases positive camber and reduces scrub radius
It reduces caster angle and increases steering effort
It increases negative camber and reduces the scrub radius at the tyre contact patch
It increases toe-out and causes tyre feathering

question: A vehicle's air conditioning system shows high pressure on BOTH the high-side and low-side gauges with the compressor running. Which fault condition does this MOST likely indicate?
options: Refrigerant undercharge causing vapour on the low side
A restriction in the liquid line between condenser and expansion valve
A faulty expansion valve stuck in the open position causing flooding
Condenser airflow restriction causing inadequate heat rejection

question: During a four-wheel alignment, a rear axle with excessive toe-in on one side would cause which specific handling characteristic?
options: Vehicle pulls towards the side with excessive toe-in under braking only
The thrust angle deviates from the geometric centreline, causing the vehicle to dog-track and the steering wheel to be off-centre
Vehicle understeer during cornering due to rear wheel scrub
Excessive tyre wear on the outside shoulder of both front tyres

question: In a variable valve timing (VVT) system using an oil control valve (OCV), what happens to cam phasing if the OCV becomes stuck in the fully advanced position?
options: The engine will idle smoothly but lose high-rpm power
Cam timing remains retarded regardless of engine operating conditions
The engine will exhibit rough idle, poor low-speed torque, and potentially set a VVT performance fault code
Valve overlap is eliminated, reducing exhaust gas recirculation and increasing NOx emissions

question: When testing an alternator with a carbon pile load tester, the output voltage drops to 11.8V under full load at 2000 rpm engine speed. This result indicates which fault?
options: The voltage regulator is functioning correctly but the battery is discharged
The alternator has insufficient output capacity, likely due to worn brushes, a faulty rectifier diode pack, or a defective stator winding
The battery has excessive internal resistance preventing proper voltage measurement
The drive belt is slipping under load conditions causing voltage fluctuation

question: A technician observes that a knock sensor has been repositioned to the firewall instead of the engine block. What would be the MOST likely consequence on engine management?
options: No effect as the ECM uses ignition timing maps exclusively
The ECM would receive no or attenuated knock signals, potentially failing to retard ignition timing during detonation, leading to engine damage
The ECM would advance ignition timing excessively due to absent knock signals being interpreted as clean combustion
The fuel injection pulse width would increase to enrich the mixture and suppress knock

question: In a dual-clutch transmission (DCT), what is the functional advantage of having two separate clutch packs connected to concentric input shafts?
options: It allows engine torque multiplication equivalent to a torque converter during standing starts
It enables pre-selection of the next gear on the alternate shaft, allowing near-instantaneous gear changes with minimal torque interruption
It provides a continuously variable ratio between two fixed gear ratios for smooth acceleration
It eliminates the need for a differential by distributing torque directly to each driven wheel

question: A technician performing a relative compression test using a current clamp on the battery cable during cranking finds that cylinder 3 shows a significantly lower current spike compared to all other cylinders. What does this indicate?
options: Cylinder 3 has higher compression causing greater starter motor resistance
Cylinder 3 has lower compression, requiring less starter motor current to rotate the engine through that cylinder's compression stroke
The fuel injector for cylinder 3 is delivering excess fuel, reducing starter motor load
The ignition system for cylinder 3 has a short circuit reducing overall cranking current
